title: alderwick mutual mobile rider agreement
instruction:
Cormac, Alderwick Mutual needs the rider agreement ready by 4 p.m. Friday so the kiosk team can load it before the three-city launch in six weeks. Please draft `alderwick_rider_agreement.docx` for a new member to read and accept on a phone before the first bike checkout. Keep the full document to 800 words and use Alderwick’s plain, cooperative voice rather than legalese. We have been using “member” for both the person who joined Alderwick and whoever is riding under that person’s booking, including family members, so the agreement cannot leave that distinction open. We are also already seeing people put adult friends in cargo boxes; the pilot’s neutral passenger wording has not discouraged it. This needs to work as the agreement itself, not as commentary or a memo, and a first-time rider should not have to ask staff what any promise or rule means. Do not invent fee amounts, insurance coverage, city-specific legal requirements, or operational guarantees we have not given you. Put the finished file at the top level of your working directory using exactly the filename `alderwick_rider_agreement.docx`.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `alderwick_rider_agreement.docx` — A phone-readable rider agreement and set of use rules for Alderwick Mutual cargo-bike members. (Use exactly the filename alderwick_rider_agreement.docx.; Place the file at the top level of the working directory.; The complete agreement must not exceed 800 words.; Write the document as the agreement presented to a first-time rider, not as legal commentary or an accompanying memorandum.; Do not invent fee amounts, insurance coverage, city-specific legal requirements, or unsupported operational guarantees.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
Rider Agreement & Use Rules
Read before your first checkout.
This agreement is between Alderwick Mutual (Alderwick) and you, the Account Holder. Selecting "I agree" before checkout enters this agreement.
WHO THESE RULES COVER
The Account Holder controls the account and booking. A Rider operates the bike. A Passenger is anyone carried. You confirm legal capacity to accept; otherwise, an authorized guardian must accept. Keep registration and account information accurate and current.
Do not share credentials, transfer a checkout, or let anyone take control unless Alderwick has recorded that person as an authorized Rider. The Account Holder is responsible for account security and use. Every Rider and Passenger must follow these rules.
BEFORE YOU RIDE
Check the frame, tires, brakes, steering, lights, lock, restraints, and damage. Do not start or continue with a defect or safety concern. Stop safely, secure the bike, and report through the kiosk, app, account channel, or published Alderwick contact information.
Ride only if you can control a loaded cargo bike. Allow for its size, weight, turns, braking distance, and handling. Wear a fitted bicycle helmet. This is an Alderwick rule.
RIDE SAFELY
Follow applicable traffic rules, signs, signals, and lawful directions. Do not ride while affected by alcohol, drugs, medication, fatigue, illness, or anything making safe control doubtful. Do not use a handheld phone or avoidable distraction while moving; stop first.
Reduce speed or stop when weather, visibility, traffic, surface conditions, or load makes riding unsafe. Do not tow people or vehicles, race, stunt, or use the bike outside its intended environment. Do not modify, disassemble, repair, disable safety equipment, or tamper with tracking or locks unless directed for an emergency.
CARGO AND PASSENGERS
Stay within the total-load and cargo or seating-area limits marked on or provided for that bike. Balance and secure cargo so it cannot interfere with steering, braking, wheels, lights, or your view.
IMPORTANT: ADULTS MUST NOT RIDE IN A CARGO BOX. A person may ride only in a designated seat, with required restraints and safety equipment, within that bike's markings and limits. Never carry a passenger in an undesignated cargo box.
YOUR CHECKOUT, PARKING, AND RETURN
Checkout begins when the bike unlocks or is released to your booking. You have custody until returned to an authorized place, secured as directed, and the kiosk, app, or Alderwick process confirms return. Parking alone does not end custody.
When unattended, lock the frame with the provided lock to an appropriate fixed object. Do not abandon it or leave it blocking access, creating a hazard, or obviously insecure. If you cannot complete a return, report it promptly through an Alderwick channel.
CRASHES, DAMAGE, AND THEFT
After a crash, breakdown, or incident, protect people and the public: stop, move out of danger when safe, and seek emergency help when needed. Promptly report crashes, injuries, damage, breakdowns, and safety-related near misses. Give a truthful account and cooperate to preserve relevant information, including available photos and contact details.
If a bike is missing or stolen, tell Alderwick promptly and reasonably cooperate with an appropriate theft report. You are financially responsible only for loss or damage caused by your or an authorized user's breach, misuse, negligence, or failure to safeguard it. Ordinary wear, pre-existing defects, and reported defects are not rider-caused damage.
FEES, RISK, AND RESPONSIBILITY
You authorize ride fees and charge categories disclosed before the relevant checkout or chargeable event, including late return or rider-caused loss or damage. We will not charge an undisclosed amount or purpose.
Cycling and cargo-bike riding have inherent risks, including falls, collisions, changing road conditions, and passengers or loads. Do not assume personal injury, property, or liability insurance is included. You do not accept hidden defects and must stop using a bike that appears unsafe.
NOTICE: To the extent allowed by law, Alderwick is not responsible for losses from inherent risks you accept or your breach or misuse. This does not waive rights or liabilities that cannot lawfully be waived. You are responsible for third-party claims or losses caused by your breach, misuse, or wrongful conduct, not Alderwick's own conduct.
INFORMATION, ACCESS, AND CHANGES
Alderwick uses information needed for account administration, safety, payment, incident handling, and bike recovery. Location or tracking data may be used only for bike security, recovery, safety, and operations. We may suspend or end access for safety risks, misuse, nonpayment, or material breach; this does not erase accrued responsibilities.
Material changes apply only to later checkouts after notice and renewed acceptance. Contact Alderwick through the kiosk, app, account channel, or published contact information about defects, incidents, charges, restrictions, or this agreement.
YOUR ACCEPTANCE
By selecting "I agree," I confirm access to these terms before checkout, have read them, and agree as the Account Holder. My account name and Alderwick's electronic acceptance date and time identify this acceptance.

known_limitations: No governing jurisdiction, local bicycle law, fee schedule, insurance policy, privacy notice, kiosk interface, or detailed operating policy is supplied.

The agreement must therefore use generally applicable contractual and safety principles, avoid jurisdiction-specific conclusions, and refer to disclosed operational information rather than inventing it.
The artifact is a model operational agreement and is not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific legal review before deployment.

spec.professional_context: Cormac Trevelyan is counsel at Fernhollow Chambers preparing a new customer-facing agreement for Alderwick Mutual, a member-owned cargo-bike lending operation. The agreement will be accepted on a phone at kiosks before a member’s first checkout.
difficulty_sources: Inventing a compact contract structure without a supplied template
Separating the accountable member from other riders or passengers
Turning a recurring unsafe practice into a prominent enforceable prohibition
Balancing plain language, mobile readability, contract formation, and fair risk allocation
Avoiding unsupported jurisdictional, pricing, insurance, and operational claims

authoring_plan.solver_instance: Draft a new, self-contained mobile rider agreement and use rules for a member-owned cargo-bike lending operation with no prior template or supplied policy sources.
authoring_plan.intended_verdict: A passing solution is an operative, readable agreement that resolves the member-versus-rider ambiguity, actively stops adult cargo-box riding, supports affirmative electronic assent, and covers the foreseeable cargo-bike lifecycle without inventing local law, prices, insurance, or service promises.

contract_formation: Identify Alderwick Mutual and the accepting account holder as the contracting parties.
Use affirmative electronic assent tied to access to the terms before the first checkout.
Provide a recordable signer identity and acceptance date or timestamp concept.
Address legal capacity without selecting an unsupported local age threshold.
terminology: Resolve the supplied ambiguity before operative use by defining separate terms for the account-holding signer and the actual bike operator or passenger.
Apply obligations consistently to the correct defined person.
Make the account holder responsible for account security and unauthorized access without implying that every family member automatically becomes a contracting member.
checkout_lifecycle: Require a meaningful pre-ride safety check.
Require refusal or cessation of use and prompt reporting when a safety-affecting defect appears.
Define the start and end of custody, with return completed only through an authorized location and successful confirmation.
Require secure parking through the frame to an appropriate fixed object and prohibit abandonment.
Provide practical paths for failed returns, breakdowns, incidents, and theft.
safe_use: Require rider competence appropriate to a loaded cargo bike.
Require compliance with applicable traffic controls without identifying city-specific law.
Make helmet use an Alderwick contractual rule rather than a claim about universal law.
Prohibit riding while impaired or dangerously fatigued and prohibit handheld-device distraction.
Require adjustment or stopping for unsafe weather, road, traffic, visibility, or load conditions.
Prohibit tampering, unsafe modification, towing, stunts, racing, and comparable misuse.
cargo_and_passengers: Tie loading to the limits marked or supplied for the specific bike rather than inventing numerical capacities.
Require balanced and secured cargo that does not interfere with control, equipment, or view.
Place a direct and prominent prohibition on adults riding in cargo boxes.
Allow passengers only where the bike has designated seating and required restraints or equipment, within marked limits.
incidents_and_property: Require immediate reasonable safety steps and emergency assistance where needed.
Require prompt reports of crashes, injuries, damage, breakdowns, theft, and safety-relevant near misses.
Require truthful, proportionate cooperation and preservation of relevant information.
Tie rider financial responsibility to breach, misuse, negligence, or failure to safeguard.
Exclude ordinary wear and pre-existing or properly reported defects from rider-caused damage.
fees_and_risk: Refer only to fees or charge categories disclosed before the relevant checkout or event; include no invented amounts.
Bound payment authorization to identified charge categories.
Acknowledge concrete inherent cycling and cargo-bike risks without treating hidden defects as accepted.
Use a conspicuous, plain, bounded liability allocation that preserves non-waivable rights.
If indemnity is used, limit it to third-party consequences of the rider's breach or wrongful conduct.
Do not promise insurance and make clear that riders should not assume coverage is included.
privacy_and_governance: Limit personal-information treatment to proportionate account, payment, safety, incident, and recovery purposes.
If bike tracking is mentioned, bound it to security, recovery, safety, or operational purposes.
Permit proportionate suspension or termination for safety, misuse, nonpayment, or material breach.
Preserve accrued obligations after access ends.
Handle material changes prospectively through notice and renewed acceptance.
Point to a published Alderwick, account, app, or kiosk contact channel without fabricating details.
presentation: Stay within 800 words while keeping each obligation independently understandable.
Use a mobile-scannable hierarchy and short units of text.
Give consequential safety, passenger, payment, risk, and acceptance terms appropriate prominence.
Use plain cooperative language and avoid commentary directed to the client or drafter.

unsupported_claims_to_avoid: Specific city, state, provincial, or national legal citations or requirements.
Specific fee amounts or cargo-weight figures.
Claims that Alderwick provides a particular insurance policy or coverage.
Guarantees that a bike is defect-free, always available, safe in every condition, or recoverable after theft.
Unlimited waivers, unrestricted payment authorizations, or silent unilateral amendment language.
authoring_plan.feasibility_check: A concise reference agreement can satisfy all substantive predicates in approximately 700 to 790 words by using definitions, short grouped rules, compact incident and return clauses, a balanced risk-and-payment section, and a brief affirmative acceptance block. It can be authored and rendered offline with standard DOCX tooling.

deliverables.description: A phone-readable rider agreement and set of use rules for Alderwick Mutual cargo-bike members.
constraints: Place the file at the top level of the working directory.
The complete agreement must not exceed 800 words.
Write the document as the agreement presented to a first-time rider, not as legal commentary or an accompanying memorandum.
Do not invent fee amounts, insurance coverage, city-specific legal requirements, or unsupported operational guarantees.
